colorway.mechanism: Each console exposes --cw-body, --cw-trim, --cw-accent (lib/colorway.ts) on its page root and on every card that stands for it. Surfaces mix the nearest --cw-accent into white in OKLab.

utilities.name: bg-tint-bold
utilities.purpose: Console heroes, lineup cards, previous/next cards. Ink text.

utilities.name: raw accent
utilities.purpose: Data marks only: sales bars, rails, milestone dots, lit sprite cells, timeline dots.

headline.purpose: Every section heading, via the shared section frame.

title.purpose: Tile, game, legacy and hotspot headings.

lede.purpose: Section ledes and tile bodies in ink-2.

label.purpose: Chips, nav, spec labels, captions; sentence case.

data.purpose: Spec figures in Geist Mono; units in sans at 0.45em.

data-inline.purpose: Years, dates, prices, region figures, citation numbers.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default for entrances, hovers, view transitions (GSAP expo.out).

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour and press states on controls.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Card lift and photo scale (1.04) on hover.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: Console photo travels from lineup card to hero (--vt-name per console).

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.purpose: Hero stagger/parallax, bars from left, rails filling, count-ups, lit cells with back.out(2).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: GSAP and Lenis never start; CSS animation/transition 0.01ms; view transition falls back to root cross-fade; pinned media stage becomes static; 3D scene still. Content is in its final state in the DOM by default.

narrative.overview:
Every console, from the 1977 Atari 2600 to the 2017 Switch, is shown the way a maker shows this year's flagship: a cut-out studio photo on a big, light, rounded stage, with generous air and one confident sentence. The ground is a near-white canvas; the colour arrives in whole blocks, never in trims. Nintendo's official site sets the colour temperament (bold rounded fields in the four face-button hues, playful demos); Apple's product pages set the motion (scroll-scrubbed reveals, expo ease-out, soft hover lifts).

Each console also owns a colour. A single custom property, its accent, tints that console's hero, its lineup card, its neighbour cards and its data marks, so a page reads as that machine's page without any per-page stylesheet. The four brand hues sign the site as a whole (wordmark dots, CTA, verdict, legacy, feature blocks); the console accent signs the machine.

Density is low and deliberate: one heading scale per section, figures shown once and drawn as what they mean, sources cited inline. The user rejected an earlier dark "store aisle" direction as too heavy and too blue; the light ground is a confirmed commitment, and the direction refuses dark neon retro, pixel fonts and card-grid catalogs.
keyCharacteristics: Light neutral ground (canvas and white) with ink text; colour lives in large rounded blocks.
Four face-button hues as the brand signature; a per-console accent as the page's own colour.
One family, Geist, in two cuts: tight display at weight 650, Mono only for figures, dates and data.
Big, concentric rounding: blocks, tiles, inner panels, pills.
Flat at rest; soft lift and scale on hover; expo ease-out everywhere.
Motion enhances content that is already in the DOM; reduced motion gets the finished state.

rules.name: The Colour Owns The Block Rule
rules.body: A brand hue or console tint fills an entire rounded block or tile. Colour is never applied as a side stripe, border accent or gradient text.

rules.name: The Fill Sets The Ink Rule
rules.body: Text colour is chosen per fill for contrast: white on red and blue; ink on yellow, green, soft fills and every console tint. White on green fails (about 2.7:1) and is never used; white on blue sits at the 4.5:1 floor, so keep text on blue at body size or larger.

rules.name: The Colorway Scope Rule
rules.body: Console colour comes only from the nearest `--cw-accent` scope, through Tint, Tint Bold, or raw accent for data marks. A new console needs a colorway entry, not new CSS.

rules.name: The Heading Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: No kicker, eyebrow or small uppercase label above a heading. The heading is the first thing in its block; context goes in the lede below it.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only where the content is a number, a date, a year or a citation. Never for prose or headings.

rules.name: The Wordmark Is The Only Tracked Caps
rules.body: Wide-tracked uppercase (0.14em) belongs to the PRESS START wordmark; the EN/ES toggle is the only other caps text, as language codes.

rules.name: The Flat Until Touched Rule
rules.body: Tiles and blocks carry no resting shadow. Lift is earned by hover, focus or being the active step.

rules.name: The Glass Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome that floats over content (header, mini-timeline) is translucent with backdrop blur and a 6% black hairline.

dos: **Do** keep the ground light: canvas #f5f5f7 and white, with ink #1d1d1f.
**Do** give colour a whole rounded block: 2.5rem islands, 1.75rem tiles.
**Do** tint console-owned surfaces from `--cw-accent` (Tint Bold for heroes and console cards, Tint for quiet panels, raw accent for data marks).
**Do** pair white text with red and blue, ink text with yellow, green, soft fills and tints.
**Do** draw a spec as what it means (grid, matrix, bar) next to its number.
**Do** cite every figure inline and flag disagreeing sources with the Disputed pill.
**Do** ship content in its final state in the DOM and let motion be an enhancement that reduced motion skips.
donts: **Don't** put a kicker, eyebrow or small uppercase label above a heading.
**Don't** add hero-metric strips; a figure appears once, in the section that explains it.
**Don't** set white text on btn-green or on any console tint.
**Don't** hard-code a console's hex in a component; read the colorway scope.
**Don't** go dark, neon or pixel-font retro; the rejected "store aisle" direction stays rejected.
**Don't** use box art, screenshots or sprites; illustrations are original abstract shapes.
